# README: `--web`, `open`, retry and failure summaries, the run-graph skill, and the smoke checklist

## What to build

Document everything the previous slices added so a user can find it from the README, which `graph-execution readme` renders. Update the usage block and table (`--web`, `open`), add a short "Starting a run from your agent" section, a "When a node fails: summary and retry" section (what a failed node is, the AI summary and verdict, `Retry` in the web page and `r`/`q` in the terminal, what retry does and what it does not do, when it is not offered), the new launcher exit code 3, the two bundled skills in the skills section, and add the manual smoke checks for the web view and retry to the existing smoke-test checklist. Text only; no code changes except the tests that read the README.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `README.md` (lines 43–120 usage and live view, 203–224 exit codes and resume, 225–247 skills, 254–288 manual smoke test) — the sections to edit; the README is rendered to `dist/README.html` by `scripts/render-readme.mjs` (heading anchors like `#the-final-step-your-branch-gets-the-changes-uncommitted` are used by in-page links; keep existing headings unchanged).
- `docs/prd/01-run-skill-and-web-view.md` (§4, §5, §6, §8 manual smoke test, §10 later) — the spec these features were built from (copy in the run's context); wording for exit codes, ssh hint, sandbox exit 3, resume.
- `src/readme/readme.test.ts` and `scripts/render-readme.mjs` — tests/rendering that read the README; make sure it still renders and any assertions on headings or content still hold.
- `src/cli.ts` — the real flag names and help text (`--web`, `open [--run <id>]`, `install skills`), so the README matches the CLI exactly.
- `PRD.md` (line 73 "Web dashboard" listed as out of scope, line 318) — the original PRD; do not edit it, but do not contradict it inside the README without saying that the web view is the run view added later.

## Patterns to follow

**README voice:** short paragraphs, fenced command blocks, tables for flags and exit codes, bold for the one thing to remember, links to in-page anchors. Mirror the existing "The live view" and "Resume" sections.

**Usage block (extend, keep the existing lines):**
```
graph-execution <tasks-dir> --spec <prd-file> --provider claude|codex|opencode|qwen [--concurrency 3] [--model <m>] [--no-merge] [--web]
graph-execution --resume [--run <id>] [--no-merge] [--web]
graph-execution open [--run <id>]
graph-execution install skills [--target agents|claude|both] [--force]
graph-execution readme [--print]
```

## Step-by-step tasks

### EDIT `README.md`

- **IMPLEMENT** (1) *Usage table:* `--web` — starts the run as a background process owned by the operating system (not by your shell or your agent), opens its live page in the browser and exits; works with `--resume`; over SSH prints the URL and an `ssh -L` hint; `open [--run <id>]` — reopens the page of a run started with `--web` while its process is alive.
  (2) *"The web view" subsection after "The live view":* the same graph as the terminal, one button (**Abort** with a confirm dialog while running, **Close** after the end), the final summary on the page, binds to `127.0.0.1` only with Host/Origin checks, stays up after the run until Close, `graph-execution open` brings it back, a closed tab does not stop the run.
  (3) *"Starting a run from your agent":* after `to-tasks` the agent asks whether to start; the `run-graph` skill runs `--web` and stops (it never monitors); launcher exit codes 0 started, 2 error (nothing started, or the run process died before its page was up, with the log tail), 3 hand-off blocked (the exact foreground command is printed to run in your own terminal); the hand-off uses `launchctl`/`systemd-run --user`/`schtasks` and falls back to a detached process.
  (4) *"When a node fails: summary and retry"* (new `##` section after "Reports that don't parse" or before "Exit codes"): a node is **failed** when it errored or used all its attempts (tasks, validation gate, validation fixer, fixer, code reviewer, live tester, apply). The tool asks the same provider and model for a short plain-language explanation and a verdict (`likely to work`, `unlikely to help`, `unclear`) and shows it on the node — advice only, one extra agent call per failure, never for Ctrl+C/Abort. **Retry**: web — click the failed node, press Retry; terminal — the view stays open after a failure, arrows pick the failed node, `r` retries, `q` quits (Ctrl+C also quits). Retry re-runs that node with its attempts reset to 0, re-entering the run like `--resume` in the same process, so tasks the failure had interrupted restart as well. Not offered after Ctrl+C/Abort (use `--resume`), after Close/`q`, for a reviewer or tester once the result was applied to your branch, or without a TTY.
  (5) *Exit codes table:* add a line for the launcher's `3` (hand-off blocked, `--web` only; nothing was started).
  (6) *Resume:* one sentence that `--resume --web` continues in the background and that Retry is the in-process equivalent while the run's process is alive.
  (7) *Skills section:* the command now installs `to-tasks` and `run-graph`; refusal is per skill folder (skipped ones are listed, exit 2 only when nothing was installed); describe `run-graph` in two bullets; the closing example becomes `npx graph-execution .agents/tasks --spec PRD.md --provider claude --web`.
  (8) *Manual smoke test:* add checks, once each on Windows, macOS and a Linux desktop, started by hand and from Claude Code and Codex: `--web` opens the page and shows the live graph; the run survives closing the agent/shell; Abort works; `--resume --web` continues; Close ends the process; `graph-execution open` reopens a live page and fails cleanly after Close; over SSH the URL and hint are printed; a strict sandbox gives exit 3 with a usable command; a task made to fail shows the AI summary and verdict, Retry (web) and `r` (terminal) re-run it and the run completes.
- **GOTCHA**: do not rename or remove existing headings; run `npm run build` to make sure `scripts/render-readme.mjs` still renders.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run build && npm test -- readme`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The usage block and options table document `--web` and `open`, matching `graph-execution --help` exactly (names, argument placeholders).
- [ ] The README explains the web view, "Starting a run from your agent", failure summaries and Retry (web and terminal), and when Retry is not offered.
- [ ] Exit code 3 is documented as the launcher's hand-off-blocked code.
- [ ] The skills section describes both bundled skills and the per-skill refusal.
- [ ] The manual smoke test lists the web, `open`, SSH, sandbox and retry checks.
- [ ] `npm run build` renders the README; `npm test -- readme` passes; no existing heading was renamed.

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run typecheck && npm run lint
npm run build
npm test -- readme
```
